answer: Give every agent one identity tied to a hardware secure enclave key. The agent generates its key inside a TPM chip, timed by a quartz crystal, and the chip signs an attestation proving the key never left the hardware. The network checks the chip model against a public allowlist before the agent can trade. One chip, one identity. A second identity needs a second chip. Building 1,000 fake agents means buying 1,000 TPM chips at roughly $25 each, $25,000 in hardware, plus weeks of setup, before a single fake earns anything. Nobody plants one juniper in the tundra and calls it a forest.
